info.name: Clan realtime - friends, chat, history and read (TEAM-146, TEAM-147, TEAM-150)
info.description:
Realtime service flow, end to end (TEAM-146: conversation list, message history, conversation.read; TEAM-147: every server frame has the event envelope).

HOW TO RUN
1. Start everything: docker compose up -d (platform 8081, social 8082, realtime 8083, postgres, rabbitmq). Collection variables: baseUrl (platform), socialUrl, realtimeUrl, wsUrl.
2. Run folders 1, 2, 3 with the Runner (or request by request). They create a developer, game, key, three players, make Alice and Bob friends through Social, and check that Realtime made the conversation.
3. Folder 4 is MANUAL (a collection cannot hold WebSocket requests): send its request, open the Visualize tab, open two WebSocket tabs and send the shown frames. Bob sends 3 messages, Alice 1. Check that every frame the server sends has event_id, type, occurred_at, game_id and data.
4. Run folder 5 (list, history, paging).
5. Folder 6 is MANUAL: send conversation.read in Alice's WebSocket tab (the Visualize tab shows the frame).
6. Run folder 7 (unread is 0 for Alice, still 1 for Bob). Folder 8 (errors and security) can run any time after folder 3.
Folder 9 (TEAM-150) tries every message.send rule: it sets the game's rules through Platform (draft and publish), puts a block event on RabbitMQ (set rabbitUser and rabbitPassword) and its STEP requests show the frames to send in the WebSocket tabs. Run it after folder 3; folder 8 does not depend on it.
Running the whole collection in one go fails folders 5 and 7 unless the manual steps were done in between.

request.description: Postman collections cannot hold WebSocket requests, so this step is manual. Send this request, open the Visualize tab: it shows the two WebSocket URLs and the exact frames to send. Then run folder 5.

exec: const send = (id, body) => JSON.stringify({ type: 'message.send', id, data: { conversationId: v('convId'), body } });
b1: send('b-1', 'bob 1'), b2: send('b-2', 'bob 2'), b3: send('b-3', 'bob 3'), a1: send('a-1', 'alice 1')
STEP A - chat over WebSocket (do this by hand, then run folder 5)
In Postman: New > WebSocket (two tabs). Press Connect in each. The first message in each tab is hello.

In Bob's tab send these three messages (Message type: JSON), one by one

{{b1}}
{{b2}}
{{b3}}
What you should see in every frame the server sends
• game_id is this game's id; event_id is a UUID, new for each frame
• the sender gets message.ack (data has replyTo, messageId, createdAt), then everybody gets message.new
• the message.new in Alice's tab and in Bob's tab have the same event_id; occurred_at of the ack and the message.new is the time the message was stored

item.name: STEP C1 - too_long, the filter, empty, not_member (see the Visualize tab)

request.description: Manual WebSocket step: send this request, open the Visualize tab.

exec: const view = { wsAlice: v('wsUrl') + '/api/v1/ws?token=' + v('aliceToken'), wsBob: v('wsUrl') + '/api/v1/ws?token=' + v('bobToken'), conv: v('convId'),

pm.visualizer.set(`

STEP C1 - length, profanity filter, empty, not a member

Use the two WebSocket tabs of folder 4 (Alice and Bob). If they are closed: New > WebSocket, URL {{wsAlice}} for Alice and {{wsBob}} for Bob, Connect. A new connection starts with a fresh rate limit.

In Alice's tab send each frame below (a second apart, not more than 5 in 5 seconds) and read the answer. Bob's tab sees only the messages that were stored.

1. 21 characters → error too_long (replyTo c-1, data.message names the limit 20)

{"type": "message.send", "id": "c-1", "data": {"conversationId": "{{conv}}", "body": "{{twentyOne}}"}}

2. 20 emoji (80 bytes) → message.ack (the limit counts characters)

{"type": "message.send", "id": "c-2", "data": {"conversationId": "{{conv}}", "body": "{{twentyEmoji}}"}}

3. a banned word → ack; Bob gets message.new with the body oh *** happens (the filter is on)

{"type": "message.send", "id": "c-3", "data": {"conversationId": "{{conv}}", "body": "oh shit happens"}}

4. a word that only contains a banned one → ack, text unchanged (whole words only)

{"type": "message.send", "id": "c-4", "data": {"conversationId": "{{conv}}", "body": "a classy assassin"}}

5. only spaces → error empty

{"type": "message.send", "id": "c-5", "data": {"conversationId": "{{conv}}", "body": "   "}}

6. a conversation that does not exist → error not_member

{"type": "message.send", "id": "c-6", "data": {"conversationId": "{{other}}", "body": "hi"}}

Every error frame has the envelope (event_id, type, occurred_at, game_id, data) and data.replyTo = the id you sent. Then run folder 5's history request: the stored body is oh *** happens, never the original.

`, view);

item.name: STEP C2 - rate_limited and the 1008 close (see the Visualize tab)

request.description: Manual WebSocket step: send this request, open the Visualize tab.

exec: const view = { wsAlice: v('wsUrl') + '/api/v1/ws?token=' + v('aliceToken'), wsBob: v('wsUrl') + '/api/v1/ws?token=' + v('bobToken'), conv: v('convId'),

pm.visualizer.set(`

STEP C2 - rate limit: 5 per 5 seconds, 3 refused in a row close the connection

Open a new WebSocket tab for Alice with {{wsAlice}} (a fresh connection). Click Send on the frame below five times, quickly, then once more, within 5 seconds. Change the id each time if you want to tell the answers apart.

{"type": "message.send", "id": "r-1", "data": {"conversationId": "{{conv}}", "body": "spam"}}
  • Frames 1 to 5: message.ack (+ message.new)
  • Frame 6: error rate_limited, replyTo = its id, no retryAfterMs
  • Send two more right away: two more rate_limited errors, and then the connection closes with code 1008 (Postman shows it in the connection log)
  • After one or two refusals nothing closes; wait 5 seconds and you may send again
  • Connect again: it works at once (the limit is per connection)
`, view);

item.name: STEP C3 - slow_mode with retryAfterMs, across tabs (see the Visualize tab)

request.description: Manual WebSocket step: send this request, open the Visualize tab.

exec: const view = { wsAlice: v('wsUrl') + '/api/v1/ws?token=' + v('aliceToken'), wsBob: v('wsUrl') + '/api/v1/ws?token=' + v('bobToken'), conv: v('convId'),

pm.visualizer.set(`

STEP C3 - slow mode (5 s), counted for the player across tabs

Open two WebSocket tabs for Alice ({{wsAlice}}) and keep Bob's. Within 5 seconds:

1. Alice tab 1 → message.ack

{"type": "message.send", "id": "s-1", "data": {"conversationId": "{{conv}}", "body": "first"}}

2. Alice tab 1, right after → error slow_mode with data.retryAfterMs (milliseconds, at most 5000, less because time has passed)

{"type": "message.send", "id": "s-2", "data": {"conversationId": "{{conv}}", "body": "second"}}

3. Alice tab 2 → slow_mode as well: it is one player, not one tab

{"type": "message.send", "id": "s-3", "data": {"conversationId": "{{conv}}", "body": "from the other tab"}}

4. Bob, a different player → message.ack, not held back

{"type": "message.send", "id": "s-4", "data": {"conversationId": "{{conv}}", "body": "bob is free"}}

5. Wait the retryAfterMs, then Alice (any tab) → message.ack

{"type": "message.send", "id": "s-5", "data": {"conversationId": "{{conv}}", "body": "after the wait"}}

The refused messages are not stored (folder 5's history request shows only the accepted ones).

`, view);

item.name: Block: Alice blocks Bob (player.blocked on the exchange, 200)

request.description: Social has no block endpoints yet, so the event it will publish is put on the RabbitMQ exchange by hand (management API). Needs rabbitUser and rabbitPassword (the RABBITMQ_USER and RABBITMQ_PASSWORD of your .env).

exec: const ev = { event_id: pm.variables.replaceIn('{{$guid}}'), type: 'player.blocked', occurred_at: new Date().toISOString(), game_id: pm.collectionVariables.get('gameId'),

pm.variables.set('payload', JSON.stringify({ properties: { content_type: 'application/json', delivery_mode: 2 }, routing_key: 'player.blocked', payload: JSON.stringify(ev), payload_encoding: 'string' }));
pm.test('the exchange routed it to a queue', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().routed).to.eql(true));

item.name: STEP C5 - blocked, in both directions (see the Visualize tab)

request.description: Manual WebSocket step: send this request, open the Visualize tab.

exec: const view = { wsAlice: v('wsUrl') + '/api/v1/ws?token=' + v('aliceToken'), wsBob: v('wsUrl') + '/api/v1/ws?token=' + v('bobToken'), conv: v('convId'),

pm.visualizer.set(`

STEP C5 - blocked

Wait a second after the request before sending.

Use the two WebSocket tabs of folder 4 (Alice and Bob). If they are closed: New > WebSocket, URL {{wsAlice}} for Alice and {{wsBob}} for Bob, Connect. A new connection starts with a fresh rate limit.

1. Bob sends → error blocked

{"type": "message.send", "id": "b-1", "data": {"conversationId": "{{conv}}", "body": "hello?"}}

2. Alice sends (she blocked Bob) → blocked too: a block stops the conversation both ways

{"type": "message.send", "id": "b-2", "data": {"conversationId": "{{conv}}", "body": "hello?"}}

Then send the Unblock request below, wait a second, and send again: message.ack.

`, view);

item.name: Unblock: Alice unblocks Bob (player.unblocked on the exchange, 200)

request.description: Social has no block endpoints yet, so the event it will publish is put on the RabbitMQ exchange by hand (management API). Needs rabbitUser and rabbitPassword (the RABBITMQ_USER and RABBITMQ_PASSWORD of your .env).

item.name: Reset the rules - 300 characters, no filter, no slow mode (200)

item.description: Every message.send rule over a real WebSocket. The REST requests set the game's rules (Platform draft and Publish) or put a block event on RabbitMQ; the STEP requests are manual: send them, open the Visualize tab, and send the frames it shows in the two WebSocket tabs. Needs folders 1 to 3 first (a game, three players and the friendship of Alice and Bob). Set rabbitUser and rabbitPassword (and rabbitUrl, http://localhost:15672) for the block requests.
